stem: Typing errors in a document follow a Poisson distribution with mean 1.5 errors per page. What is the probability that a randomly chosen page has at least 1 typing error? [Given: e^(-1.5) = 0.2231]

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.2231 = P(X=0) = e^(-1.5); the student found the probability of zero errors instead of the complement (at least one).
0.3347 = P(X=1) = e^(-1.5)*1.5 = 0.2231*1.5 = 0.3347; the student computed exactly one error rather than at least one.
0.5578 = P(X=0)+P(X=1) = 0.2231+0.3347 = 0.5578; the student summed P(0) and P(1) instead of computing 1 - P(0).

explanation: P(at least 1) = 1 - P(X=0) = 1 - e^(-lambda) = 1 - e^(-1.5) = 1 - 0.2231 = 0.7769. Use the complement rule for at-least-one problems.

explanation_sections.punchline: At-least-one equals the complement of zero; one subtraction replaces summing infinitely many terms.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: Poisson(lambda=1.5). Identify: at least 1 means complement of X=0. P(X=0)=e^(-1.5)=0.2231. P(X>=1)=1-0.2231=0.7769.
explanation_sections.lesson: For Poisson at-least-one questions, always use the complement: P(X>=1) = 1 - e^(-lambda).
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. One subtraction; use the given hint. Trap: choosing e^(-1.5) directly or computing P(X=1) only.
